content: The latest discovery from NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover is a field of honeycomb-shaped polygons covering a Martian valley called Valle Grande. As Gizmodo reports, Curiosity has snapped pictures of the unusual terrain texture before, called polygonal fractures, each about 1.5 to 3 inches wide, but NASA says it’s previously only found them in small patches, “nothing on the scale discovered in Valle Grande.”  Curiosity captured a 360-degree panorama of the “sea of polygons” on June 19th and 20th (Martian sols 4,930 and 4,931) that shows the texture spreading out in all directions. Project scientist Ashwin Vasavada says the Curiosity team “measured their shapes and chemistry carefully and are hopeful there are clues in the data as to how these features formed.”  NASA says billions of years ago, “lakes and streams dappled the lower foothills of Mount Sharp, a 3-mile-tall (5-kilometer-tall) mountain that Curiosity has been ascending since 2014.” This terrain could also indicate there was once water in Valle Grande, based on previous polygon patches: > Some of the polygons that the mission has spotted in the past clearly formed as mud cracks, though a variety of processes can contribute to their honeycomb textures, including cycles of warm and cold temperatures or compression that squeezed water out of the sediment when the surface was buried.

chineseContent: 美国宇航局好奇号火星探测器的最新发现是一片蜂窝状多边形区域，覆盖着一个名为格兰德谷的火星山谷。据 Gizmodo 报道，好奇号之前曾拍摄过这种不寻常的地形纹理的照片，称为多边形裂缝，每个裂缝约 1.5 至 3 英寸宽，但 NASA 表示，之前只发现了小块碎片，“在格兰德谷还没有发现过如此规模的裂缝”。  好奇号于 6 月 19 日至 20 日（火星太阳公历 4,930 和 4,931）拍摄到了“多边形海洋”的 360 度全景图，显示纹理向各个方向扩散。项目科学家阿什温·瓦萨瓦达 (Ashwin Vasavada) 表示，好奇号团队“仔细测量了它们的形状和化学成分，并希望数据中能提供有关这些特征如何形成的线索。”  NASA 表示，数十亿年前，“夏普山的低山麓上布满了湖泊和溪流，夏普山是一座 3 英里高（5 公里高）的山峰，好奇号自 2014 年以来一直在攀登这座山。”根据之前的多边形斑块，该地形还可能表明格兰德谷曾经有过水： > 任务过去发现的一些多边形显然是由泥裂形成的，尽管多种过程可以促成它们的蜂窝状纹理，包括冷暖温度的循环或在表面被掩埋时将水从沉积物中挤出的压缩。
